specification.outcome: A user can create an ordinary Backlog task or replace an existing Backlog task's canonical specification through normal conversation, without a campaign and without implicitly beginning work.

scenarios.name: create an ordinary unspecified backlog task
given: the request contains a title and description that pass the existing task semantic parsers
the signed task board is writable
when: the user asks Pi in normal conversation to create a ticket without supplying a complete specification
then: the host generates the task and event identifiers and publishes one signed ordinary task-created event
the canonical task metadata is the host-normalized title and description
the task is unclaimed and unspecified in Backlog with no campaign provenance

scenarios.name: atomically create a specified backlog task
given: the request contains valid task metadata and a complete specification that passes parseTaskSpecification
the signed task board is writable
when: the user asks Pi to create the specified ticket
then: one fast-forward publication atomically contains creation and specification events or one equivalent closed compound event
the observable board never contains a partial task if signing or publication fails
the task remains unclaimed in Backlog without readiness review, ordering changes, or campaign provenance

scenarios.name: amend only an existing backlog specification
given: the target task exists unclaimed in Backlog
the host binds the observed verified board head and current specification digest, including none, before attempting publication
when: the user asks Pi to replace its canonical specification with a value that passes parseTaskSpecification
then: one signed fast-forward publication replaces only the canonical specification and digest
task identity, title, description, Backlog state, claim state, Ready ordering, priority, and campaign provenance are preserved
no readiness review, claim, run journal, or worktree is created

scenarios.name: reject invalid create requests and publication authority failures
given: an ordinary create-task request is malformed, the board is read-only, signing is unavailable, or publication cannot fast-forward
then: it applies denial precedence TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED, then TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT
no partial task or specification event is observable
a stale-head conflict may be retried only after a fresh board observation while every bound input remains unchanged

scenarios.name: reject invalid specification amendments
given: a specify-task request is malformed, the board is read-only, the task is missing, the task is not unclaimed Backlog, or the replacement specification is invalid
then: it applies denial precedence TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID, TIBER_TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TIBER_TASK_NOT_FOUND, TIBER_TASK_LIFECYCLE_INVALID, then TIBER_SPECIFICATION_INVALID
no task event, readiness review, claim, run journal, campaign checkpoint, or worktree effect occurs

scenarios.name: reject a concurrent stale amendment
given: the host bound an expected board head and current specification digest
another writer publishes a newer specification for the same task before this publication
when: the host observes the fast-forward conflict and refreshes signed state
then: it returns TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT without applying the stale replacement
the newer specification remains authoritative and retry requires a newly evaluated user request

scenarios.name: route ordinary language independently of campaigns
given: the user asks to create a ticket or edit a Backlog specification
no campaign exists or an unrelated campaign is active
when: Pi infers the corresponding workflow request
then: the closed request is create-task or specify-task rather than campaign-goal or begin-task
campaign state is neither required nor changed

acceptanceCriteria: create-task is a closed request with title, description, and an optional complete TaskSpecification; absence of a specification intentionally creates an unspecified task and metadata never masquerades as a specification.

specify-task is a closed request with task identity and a complete replacement TaskSpecification; the host binds the currently observed board head and specification digest as publication preconditions.
Task text and specifications are parsed once into existing semantic values; publication uses host-canonical semantic JSON and its computed digest rather than requiring byte-identical model input.
Atomic specified creation cannot expose a task without its requested specification after any signing, push, race, or retry failure.
Ordinary create and specify operations never promote, prioritize, review, claim, start, or create campaign provenance.
Stable typed denials and precedence are tested at the public workflow-request boundary.
Signed publication remains fast-forward-only and a concurrent amendment can never silently overwrite a newer specification.
exclusions: Changing title or description after creation
Automatically starting, reviewing, ranking, or claiming tasks
Changing campaign scheduling or goal semantics
Weakening signature, ancestry, or lifecycle verification
specification.architectureImplications: Extend the closed workflow request algebra and deterministic host dispatcher with create-task and specify-task effects. The host owns identifier generation, parse-once canonicalization, expected-head and expected-specification preconditions, atomic event publication, signing, conflict observation, and receipts. Inference supplies semantic intent but cannot grant authority, retry across changed task state, or trigger readiness and work effects.
